title: Stanford's Dr. Karan: Hantavirus Is No COVID Panic
excerpt: The Indian-American infectious disease expert urges calm as a deadly cruise ship outbreak triggers pandemic fears across the US.
body:
Dr. Abraar Karan, an infectious disease physician and faculty member at Stanford University, stepped forward this week to cut through the noise — telling Americans that the hantavirus outbreak linked to the cruise ship MV Hondius does not warrant the pandemic-level alarm spreading across social media and cable news.

**What the outbreak actually looks like:**
A cluster of cases tied to the Dutch ship MV Hondius prompted a global contact-tracing effort after the WHO confirmed the Andes strain of hantavirus on May 2, 2026. As of May 8, eight cases were reported — six confirmed, three fatal. A Santa Clara County resident who was aboard the ship returned home and is being actively monitored by state and county health officials in coordination with the CDC. Karan said officials 'know who we are monitoring, we know what virus we are dealing with,' adding that he does not expect further spread because any symptomatic person would immediately be isolated.

**Why this is not a repeat of 2020:**
The WHO's Maria van Kerkhove said flatly, 'This is not SARS-CoV-2 and not the start of a COVID pandemic.' The CDC classified its response as Level 3 — its lowest emergency tier. On average, an infected person spreads hantavirus to fewer than one other person; COVID-19, by contrast, infected multiple people per case. The Andes virus requires close, prolonged contact — among household members, intimate partners, or caregivers — to transmit person-to-person, and the CDC confirmed that no cases have been reported inside the United States as a result of this outbreak. Routine travel, the agency said, can continue as normal.

**What to watch next:**
Public health experts continue to flag concern not about hantavirus itself, but about the CDC's muted public communication — a pattern some attribute to deep federal staffing cuts — and whether that silence will leave Americans underinformed when a more serious threat eventually arrives.
